newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan shilling firm vs dollar, sterling.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan shilling firm vs dollar, sterling.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was firm against the dollar and sterling on Tuesday in lacklustre trading, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 53.88 against the dollar, compared to 53.89 on Monday. Against sterling, the bank posted a mean of 87.35, from 87.42.
Dealers said despite a dull beginning to the week, activity appeared to have picked up on Tuesday with oil importers sniffing around for dollars at the 54 level.
Some dealers said they were trading cautiously as the market was still vulnerable to large volumes.
"The shilling is holding at the 53.70/54.10 level. Whether it will break the 54 level, a psychological barrier, will depend on inflows from coffee and tea sales today," one dealer said.
The money market tightened slightly on tax outflows. Overnight rates were quoted between 13 and 16 percent, compared to below 10 percent on Monday.
